layers.note: A tufted grass of the herb layer.

moisture.note: Wet meadows, marsh edges and streambanks, and moist open ground; not dry sites.

heat_load.note: Indifferent to aspect wherever it is wet enough.

elevation_m.note: From sea level to alpine meadows.

max_slope_deg.note: Mostly level or gently sloping wet ground.

shade_tolerance.note: Needs open or lightly shaded ground.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −30 °C, gone by −40 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −50 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −60 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 6 to 24 °C; gone below 3 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: Across its range, about 500 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 200.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 150 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 20.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No limit: it grows under summer-dry and summer-wet climates alike.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in western Washington lowland forests; not yet checked against Silvics of North America (Burns and Honkala, 1990) or the Fire Effects Information System, both public-domain USDA Forest Service works. Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Tufted hairgrass is circumpolar, from tidal marshes to alpine meadows (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
